answer: Agents must lock a bond before earning rewards, and independent audits slash it when multiple identities reuse the same work or coordinate false claims. Tasks come from a public garden, but hidden tests check each result; a ferrous-backed registry also limits each credential to one active bond. A sybil attacker must fund many agents and keep them capable across varied tests, risking every bond if coordination is detected. Yarrow-marked tasks can rotate in to defeat copied scripts.
